observations.explanation: Table 1 reports pass@5 gains for DeepSeek, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 on both validation and test sets, including GPT-4 validation rising from 19% to 44% (PDF p. 7).
The paper describes preprocessing and code-iteration stages, running and fixing code against public and AI-generated tests, and using test anchors to preserve previously passed tests (PDF pp. 3–6).

The authors explicitly note evaluation subtleties and say AlphaCode and CodeChain did not release reproducible end-to-end generation and evaluation scripts, which supports the qualified concern about direct comparisons (PDF p. 7).

The supplied results report aggregate flow performance but no component-wise ablation isolating individual stages or design concepts; the paper also says some stages can be combined into one LLM call (PDF pp. 5, 7; see also pp. 9–10).
